recipes.name: Broccoli Casserole
ingredients_raw: 2 (10 ounce) packages chopped frozen broccoli, thawed
1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Cut 2 tablespoons butter into small pieces; set aside.
Melt remaining 3 tablespoons butter in a medium skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion and sauté until golden, 7 to 9 minutes.

Transfer onion to a 2-quart casserole dish. Stir in broccoli, condensed soup, Cheddar, mayonnaise, eggs, lemon juice, garlic salt, seasoned salt, and pepper until well combined. Sprinkle crushed crackers over top and dot with reserved butter.
Bake, uncovered, in the preheated oven until heated through and browned on top, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Broccoli Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This tasty broccoli and cheese casserole made with simple ingredients comes together quickly for a comfort-food meal the whole family will love.

review.reviewBody: This is VERY close to a recipe I used to make and have been searching for-- with the following changes: 1) instead of cooking fresh onion, dried chopped onion can be substituted (the liquids in the dish will reconstitue it,) 2) instead of cream of mush, use cream of celery soup, 3) lose all that salt and just use a little garlic powder, plus a dash or two of worcestershire instead of the lemon juice, and, 4) top with crushed cheez-its instead of Ritz-- the extra cheddar crunch gives the entire dish a great zing (go crazy-- tabasco cheez-its are expecially good.) No need to top with butter, the topping will brown nicely enough. You can adjust the fat content by eliminating the butter and using low-fat soup. I also use the canola Hellman's with no cholesterol. Ditching the salt brings the sodium content down to next-to-nothing, even with the modicum of worcestershire. When all is said and done, what you're really making here is a custard-- that's why you mix the soup, eggs, and mayo together and then fold in the broccoli and the cheese. It should never be runny. The entire casserole can be assembled the day before and refrigerated, then the topping added right before cooking. Enjoy!

I really liked this recipe as a starting point but, I admit I never had the intentiom of following it to a 'T'. I didn't add as much mayonaisse as the cripe calls for and added raw cubed chicken tenders to the mix. I made it with gluten free crackers so I used much more than the recipe (enough to completely cover the top layer). It was good but I can see how some of the other reviews said it was too liquidy. I was glad I added the chicken.

The second time I baked it, I substituted half of the mayo with sour cream, added 1/2 cup of Colby jack cheese, added 1/2tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tap chili powder, and little extra salt and pepper as well (note: I never used garlic salt. Only powder). I found this to be a better recipe.

I baked it on the middle rack for 30 minutes and placed it on the top rack for the remaining 15 for a nice golden crisp. Adjust that last 15 minutes to your liking.

I don't usually like mushroom soup in this type of casserole, but with the other additions to the sauce, you couldn't even taste the mushroom soup. I used fresh broccoli (parboiled) and had matchstick carrots I needed to use, so I sauteed them with the onions. It added great taste, texture, and color. The crumb topping was nice and crunchy. It reminds me of a casserole my sister used to make called Muzzie Casserole. Delicious!

After a few changes this is one I will keep as a favorite. Instead of garlic salt I sautéed chopped garlic with the onion. Also I added chopped mushrooms to the mix. Then once the mix was in the pan I covered it with crushed Annie’s Organic Cheddar crackers.

GREEN BEAN CASSAROLE-MOVE OVER! New family favorite, I followed the recipe in spirit. I substituted worcestershire for lemon juice, used fresh blanched broccoli, sauteed fresh garlic with the onion and sliced mushrooms, kept the mayo/eggs/mushroom soup but added 1/2 cup of instant rice to absorb extra moisture and add texture, and topped with 3 cooked crumbled bacon strips and extra cheese instead of cracker crumbs. YUM,YUM,YUM

It was ok...too much mayonnaise & the egg felt scrambled inside...not a good thing texture wise. I will try it again but mix everything in a separate bowl, use less mayonnaise & salt, & maybe use fresh broccoli.
I made a half portion and left out the onion. It came out watery. I made it again. I drained the broccoli well this time. I used scallions instead of regular onions. I really liked it this time.

this recipe is so yummy! my whole family loves it! I like to add shredded cooked chicken to this and then its the main dish! Also I don't bother to cook the onion.......I find it easier and perhaps even more flavorful. I like to use spiced breadcrumbs for the topping too!
enjoy!

I made this and it turned out great. I didn't use mayonnaise or cream of mushroom, instead i used 1.5 - 2 cups of heavy cream instead. I also substituted the Ritz crackers with Cheezits as one other person had suggested, and covered with foil the entire cooking time. It's so easy I will make this again.

This was okay. I did take suggestions and cut the salt back to none. Sauteed the onion and added shallot and garlic in butter (because I had them) with added mushroom. Blanched fresh broccoli and cauliflower and tossed that into the whipped egg, mayo, cheese, Worcestershire (vs lemon) and garlic powder. I used cream of celery, where I normally never use canned soups, but it was okay. Toped with the cracker crumbs and parsley. Made a nice side for blackened catfish and boiled potatoes.
I added 1 more cup of cheese & used fresh broccoli crown

Great recipe, super easy and I loved the flavors. I added fresh minced garlic to the onions and made my own crumb topping with sourdough bread. I also used only 1/2 cup of mayonnaise and 1 egg. It was delicious!
Followed it exactly! I have cooked allot of broccoli casseroles and this one bets them all! My husband absolutely loved it, this is the first he has gone back for refills!
Loved it! So did family, left out Mayo.
Really good. Followed exactly, but substituted 12 Oz of chicken for 10 Oz of broccoli, used only 1 bag of frozen broccoli.
I've made different variations of this recipe many times. The lemon juice was a nice addition.
This recipe is a keeper. Family loved it.
